candidate_worker_question: What hard boundary should Step 6 preserve around fallback executability and Silva/data constraint retesting before recommending any trigger-based dissertation plan?
reason: Fallback viability and Silva/data access are binding-constraint questions that a compact boundary worker can make harder for Step 6 to blur.
expected_artifact_contribution: A dated fallback-executability gate plus a separate Silva/data retest with concrete evidence needed to relax the boundary.
unnecessary_if: Step 6 already states fallback executability and Silva/data retesting as hard constraints rather than soft cautions.
kill_condition: Stop the worker if it summarizes dissertation options or advises the student instead of producing a boundary/evidence gate.

source_excerpts.text: Third-year PhD student has a 3-month direction deadline, advisor retires in 2-3 years, and the lab lacks single-cell experience or collaborators.
Pressure check says the retiring advisor is not neutral and option 1 may stop being a real fallback after enough option-3 work.
Silva/data access is unproven and controls whether the single-cell/foundation-model route is executable.
